answer: An escalating time-locked bond stops a sybil spiral: every identity must lock a deposit for 30 epochs before it can earn, and the price climbs with each identity funded from the same source — the first locks 10 units, the tenth locks 100. Like a trellis, the bond gives honest newcomers a fixed, climbable path, while a terrace of rising prices makes bulk identities uneconomic: doubling fake identities more than doubles the locked capital, and one proven duplicate forfeits the whole bond. Honest agents pay once and wait; attackers pay per identity, forever.
